subject: Phased integration runbook & canary safety nets for MeridianBank LLM deployment
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Phased integration runbook & canary safety nets for MeridianBank LLM deployment

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per Meridian's RFP ask, attached is an initial phased-integration runbook that maps our recommended sequence for development -> pilot -> production, plus a canary safety-net schedule and rollback triggers. High-level callouts below:

- Timeline: 6 weeks from signed SOW to pilot start (detailed week-by-week milestones in the PDF).
- Integration steps: VPC peering and firewall rules, mutual TLS for the inference endpoints, prefix cache warm-up plan, and a staged schema migration for embeddings.
- Canary cadence: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% over a multi-day window with automated health gates (latency, error rate, regression on our reference prompts).
- Rollback triggers: >3% error rate increase vs baseline for 30m, persistent QoE drop in evaluation harness, or SLO breach on 95th p50 latency.
- Security & audit: we include an optional audit log forwarder for SIEM ingest and retention guidance compatible with Meridian's policy.

Attachments: MERIDIAN_RFP_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook), network-integration-diagram.png.

Next steps: can you confirm a 4-hour maintenance window on a weekday evening for the pilot cutover? Also: please confirm whether the pilot will use Meridian-managed outbound NAT (preferred) or if Redwood should provision a static egress IP from our Dedicated pool.

I cc'd Karthik and Monica — Karthik can add tech-level notes, Monica will own the mutual action plan and acceptance criteria.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com

Vanessa —

Appreciate the detailed runbook. A few clarifying questions before we share with our security and procurement committees:

1) Session affinity / user routing: what does Redwood recommend for sticky sessions if we route inference via our internal load balancer? Will KV cache warming be affected?
2) Audit logs: minimum retention you support for the forwarder? We typically require 7 years for certain product telemetry; can you outline tiered retention and export options?
3) Pilot acceptance: your runbook mentions "evaluation harness" — can you share the exact acceptance thresholds (latency, top-k quality checks) used to declare pilot success?
4) Contracting: procurement needs a pilot term (we proposed 60 days) and an acceptance sign-off flow. If pilot succeeds, we expect a 6-12 month committed Dedicated capacity proposal.

Also, for the egress question: Meridian prefers outbound traffic through our managed NAT gateway.

Alex

Alex —

Thanks — good to know about the NAT. Inline answers and an updated cadence spreadsheet attached (k8s-canary-schedule.xlsx):

1) Session affinity / KV cache: we recommend session routing only for flows that require per-session KV state. For general inference requests, we use stateless JWT-based routing and seed the prefix cache during pilot with a "warm-up sweep" to prepopulate popular prompts. The runbook lists a warm-up job that runs 24h prior to pilot. If you require strict sticky sessions, we can support a routed affinity layer but that reduces batching efficiency (cost+latency tradeoff noted in section 3.2).

2) Audit logs: Redwood supports tiered retention policies. Default: 90 days immediate access + archival export to S3 (customer-managed) for up to 7 years. For >7 years we can provide legal-hold export packages. We'll include retention config in SOW.

3) Pilot acceptance thresholds (short):
   - 95th percentile latency <= 350ms for the pilot traffic profile
   - Error rate delta <= 0.5% vs baseline model for reference prompts
   - Quality regression: automated eval set mean score drop <= 2 points (we'll share the eval harness and scoring rubric)

4) Pilot term / contracting: 60 days is reasonable. Proposed acceptance flow: engineering smoke tests (7 days), joint evaluation window (21 days), final business sign-off (1 week). Monica will draft the mutual action plan and acceptance checklist and attach to the SOW.

Proposed maintenance window for pilot cutover: Tue 2027-07-06, 22:00–02:00 EDT (we'll patch in fallback DNS TTLs so rollback takes <10m to complete). Can you confirm?

Thanks — attaching k8s-canary-schedule.xlsx for the staged percentages and gating metrics.

Best,
Vanessa

Alex / team —

Quick tech note to add to the runbook (forwarding for visibility):

- KV cache warm-up: our recommended warm-up includes a two-pass strategy; first pass seeds top-500 queries from production logs (read-only ingestion), second pass simulates user traffic at 10% of pilot QPS to validate cache hit-stability. This reduces cold-start error spikes during the 1% -> 5% shift.
- Quantization profile: for Meridian's medium-latency SLA, propose int8-quantized weights with mixed-precision kernels on T4/RTX-class instances; this provides a ~2x throughput gain with negligible QoE delta in our evals. We'll surface the exact benchmark numbers in the FAQ.
- Smoke endpoints: add a /healthz/model and /healthz/eval endpoints that report model-version, kv-cache-hit, and recent eval score. Canary gating will pull these every 30s.

I'll fold these into MERIDIAN_RFP_runbook_v2 and share once Alex confirms the maintenance window.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
VP, Platform Integrations, Redwood Inference
